how_to_use: Give each case's 'input' to a fresh agent that follows the skill. Cases with kind 'repo' need the named repo on disk. Cases with kind 'pasted' are self-contained.
generic_checks: Output has Summary (case count, Target for testing, Evidence level, what was read), Questions, and Test cases, in that order. Security notes appear only when needed.
Every case heading is '### QA-NNN — Title'. ID and Title are not repeated as fields.
Every case has Priority, Platform, Precondition, Test Data, Steps, Expected Result, Basis, Status, with Steps and Expected Result as numbered lists.
Status is always 'Not run'. No case is marked passed.
Expected results describe what a tester sees. No code, function names or HTTP status codes unless the UI shows them.
No message, number, limit or rule is invented. Visible text is copied exactly from the evidence.
Evidence level says 'from code only' or names a real build check.
No secret, real email or password appears. Placeholders such as qa.user.1@example.test are used.
Markdown cases and CSV rows list the same IDs in the same order. CSV header is exact.

cases.input: Repo: /Users/ocgt/Desktop/hafizu-portfolio (read-only). Write manual QA test cases for commit 8f36d4b on master (use git show). Do not open .env* files, do not modify anything.
checks: Cases cover the skills badge (/api/badge?kind=skills), the home page skills section, the badge preview page and the status badge default 'Not open to work'.
README, docs and .env.example edits produce no case of their own.
Status-default case carries 'Applies when BADGE_STATUS is not set' and the env state is asked under Questions. No .env file was opened.
Priority for badge and preview cases is Medium or Low, not High.
The hard-coded '04 skills' header next to the shared array appears under Questions as a drift risk, or is handled with a sound reason.
Cache lifetimes (1 hour, 5 minutes) are listed under Questions as technical verification, not as cases.
Rendered text drawn into the badge image is quoted from code and not claimed to have exact casing or layout.

cases.input: Repo: /Users/ocgt/Desktop/hafizu-portfolio (read-only). Write manual QA test cases for commit 7e11701 (use git show). Do not open .env* files, do not modify anything.
checks: Near-identical badge kinds get one case each when their data source or env state differs.
Env-dependent badges (status, currently, contributions, streak, projects) carry 'Applies when ...' and the env state is asked under Questions.
Dynamic text (clock time, scores, counts) is written as a pattern, not a fixed value.
No case is above Medium priority for a README badge surface.
Cache headers, image size and timeouts are under Questions as technical verification.
A host mismatch between README and docs, if noticed, appears under Questions as a drift risk.

Cases follow the code: the fifth wrong password still shows 'Email or password is incorrect.' (the lock is set after the message is chosen), and the lockout message 'Too many attempts. Try again in 15 minutes.' appears from the sixth attempt. A case that claims the lockout message on the fifth attempt fails.
A High-priority case covers the lockout message with exact text.
A case covers a wrong password below the limit showing 'Email or password is incorrect.'.
A boundary or reset case (success before the limit resets the count) is present or justified.
Lock expiry is either a case with a stated 15-minute wait or a Question about clock control. Edge timing (just before or exactly at 15 minutes) is under Questions.
The hard-coded '15 minutes' in the UI message next to LOCK_MINUTES in the code is noted as a drift risk, or the count reset on expiry is questioned.
Target for testing says build unknown and names the diff as the source reviewed.
Test data uses a placeholder account and a fake password, never real values.
No manual case asserts an HTTP status or JSON body as the expected result.
The endpoint check is listed under Questions as 'Technical verification' and asks for an automated check or a user-facing path.
Summary says that no runnable user-facing case is supported (or equivalent), and the CSV has only the header row.
The 50-character limit is not turned into a visible UI message, since no UI evidence exists.

cases.input:
A developer sent this handoff. Review it and write the manual QA test cases that a tester can run.

1) Verify the save endpoint returns HTTP 409 on a conflicting edit. (Code: when the API returns 409 the editor shows the message "Someone else edited this. Reload to continue.")
2) Verify the lodash dependency was upgraded.
3) Check the push notification on a locked phone. (No device, build or account setup is described.)
4) README updated with the new setup steps.
checks: Item 1 becomes a user journey that checks the visible message 'Someone else edited this. Reload to continue.' The HTTP 409 is not the expected result.
Item 2 is not a case. It appears under Questions (CI or build evidence) or is dropped with a reason.
Item 3 is not a runnable case. Questions names the device, build, account and notification setup needed.
Item 4 produces no case.
A conflict case needs two users or two sessions, and the aliases are defined once in Summary.
